{
  "summary": "This pull request updates the depends build system to use content addressing rather than filesystem timestamps for packages built from a local directory. It generates a normalized tarball via CMake with a fixed timestamp on evaluation and stores it under a filename keyed by its SHA256 hash. This guarantees that local package recipe hashes and build artifacts update whenever directory contents, permissions, or symlinks change.",
  "problem": "Depends currently relies on timestamp comparisons (`find -newer`) to decide whether to rebuild local source archives (currently used by `native_libmultiprocess`). This fails to detect deleted files, files checked out with older timestamps, and changes across multiple Git worktrees sharing a single `SOURCES_PATH`, causing depends to compile stale sources.",
  "evidence": [
    "Commit b1f79c9fa6 states: 'Timestamp comparisons can reuse an archive produced by another worktree, causing Depends to build stale local sources... A tarball created by one worktree may be newer than every path in another. Deleting a file leaves no path whose mtime can be checked. Changed or restored files may have older or equal mtimes.'",
    "Linked issue #35764 reports: 'depends: `local_dir` cache invalidation can miss source changes'."
  ],
  "dependencies": {
    "depends_on": [],
    "enables": []
  },
  "scope_notes": "The implementation introduces a small CMake helper script (`depends/local_source.cmake`) invoked via `cmake -P` from `depends/funcs.mk` to ensure portable, normalized tarball generation across host platforms.",
  "changed_since_previous": "",
  "card": "This pull request changes the depends build system to content-address source archives built from local directories instead of relying on filesystem timestamp checks. Currently, packages sourced from local directories (specifically native_libmultiprocess) can fail to rebuild when files are modified, deleted, or shared across multiple git worktrees using a common sources directory because timestamp comparisons reuse stale archives. The change uses CMake to generate a normalized archive with fixed timestamps, hashes its contents, and caches it under a content-derived filename so distinct worktrees can coexist cleanly. According to the author, timestamp invalidation fails across worktrees and cannot detect deleted files or restored files with older timestamps. It has no PR dependencies.",

result.summary: This pull request updates the depends build system to use content addressing rather than filesystem timestamps for packages built from a local directory. It generates a normalized tarball via CMake with a fixed timestamp on evaluation and stores it under a filename keyed by its SHA256 hash. This guarantees that local package recipe hashes and build artifacts update whenever directory contents, permissions, or symlinks change.
result.problem: Depends currently relies on timestamp comparisons (`find -newer`) to decide whether to rebuild local source archives (currently used by `native_libmultiprocess`). This fails to detect deleted files, files checked out with older timestamps, and changes across multiple Git worktrees sharing a single `SOURCES_PATH`, causing depends to compile stale sources.
evidence: Commit b1f79c9fa6 states: 'Timestamp comparisons can reuse an archive produced by another worktree, causing Depends to build stale local sources... A tarball created by one worktree may be newer than every path in another. Deleting a file leaves no path whose mtime can be checked. Changed or restored files may have older or equal mtimes.'
Linked issue #35764 reports: 'depends: `local_dir` cache invalidation can miss source changes'.
result.scope_notes: The implementation introduces a small CMake helper script (`depends/local_source.cmake`) invoked via `cmake -P` from `depends/funcs.mk` to ensure portable, normalized tarball generation across host platforms.
result.card: This pull request changes the depends build system to content-address source archives built from local directories instead of relying on filesystem timestamp checks. Currently, packages sourced from local directories (specifically native_libmultiprocess) can fail to rebuild when files are modified, deleted, or shared across multiple git worktrees using a common sources directory because timestamp comparisons reuse stale archives. The change uses CMake to generate a normalized archive with fixed timestamps, hashes its contents, and caches it under a content-derived filename so distinct worktrees can coexist cleanly. According to the author, timestamp invalidation fails across worktrees and cannot detect deleted files or restored files with older timestamps. It has no PR dependencies.
